st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and bell pepper for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, [[1 tbsp]] paprika, [[1 tsp]] cumin and [[0.25 tsp]] cayenne and stir 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes and add [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Make 6 wells in the sauce with a spoon and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft. Cook longer for firm yolks.
Sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] parsley and serve in the pan with bread.

ing: soaked overnight in water, drained, not canned
st: Pulse the soaked chickpeas in a food processor to a coarse, crumbly texture. Do not make a paste.
Add the onion, garlic, [[1 cup]] parsley and [[0.5 cup]] cilantro and pulse until finely chopped and green.
Mix in [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] coriander, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] baking powder.
Chill 30 minutes. If it falls apart when pressed, mix in [[3 tbsp]] flour.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a pot to 350°F (175°C).
Shape the mixture into balls the size of walnuts.
Fry 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve in pita with salad and tahini.
Blend [[0.5 cup]] tahini and [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute.
Add the garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] cumin and [[1 tsp]] salt and blend 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas and blend 2 minutes, scraping the sides.
With the machine on, add [[4 tbsp]] ice water until very smooth and fluffy.
Taste and adjust salt or lemon.
Spread onto a plate with the back of a spoon, making a well.
Drizzle with [[3 tbsp]] olive oil and a pinch of paprika.
Salt the eggplant slices with [[1 tsp]] salt and leave 15 minutes. Pat dry.
Fry in [[0.5 cup]] oil over medium heat 4 minutes per side until golden and soft. Drain.
Boil the 4 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] tahini, [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[3 tbsp]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with [[2 tbsp]] parsley.
Warm the pita and spread with [[1 cup]] hummus divided between them.
Fill with eggplant, sliced egg and salad and drizzle with tahini.
Dice the cucumbers, tomatoes and onion into pieces about 0.25 inch wide.
Combine them in a large bowl.
Add [[0.25 cup]] parsley.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, [[0.75 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss.
Serve right away, or rest 10 minutes to let flavors blend.
Mix [[4 cup]] flour, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1.5 cup]] warm water into a soft dough. Knead 8 minutes and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and brush with a little of the [[1 cup]] butter. Rest another 30 minutes.
Roll one ball very thin on an oiled surface, spread with butter, and roll up like a cigar, then coil loosely.
Repeat the rolling, buttering and coiling with the other balls.
Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C). Pack the coils snugly in a covered heavy pot with [[2 tbsp]] hot water.
Bake covered for 5 hours until deep golden brown.
Boil the eggs 10 minutes and grate the tomatoes.
Serve the jachnun hot with the egg and grated tomato.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 cup]] warm water into a soft dough.
Knead 5 minutes, then rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls and roll each very thin.
Spread each with [[0.5 cup]] butter total, then roll up into a rope, coil, and flatten again.
Rest the coils for 30 minutes.
Roll each into a thin round of about 8 inches.
Fry in [[3 tbsp]] oil over medium heat 3 minutes per side until golden and flaky.
Crush a bit with your hands to flake layers.
Serve with the eggs and grated tomato.
Mix [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] turmeric, [[2 tsp]] paprika, [[0.5 tsp]] cinnamon and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Add half the garlic, [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice and [[3 tbsp]] oil to make a marinade and coat the chicken. Marinate at least 1 hour.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] tahini with the rest of the garlic and [[3 tbsp]] water until pourable.
Heat a large skillet over high heat and cook the chicken in two batches, 5 to 6 minutes each, until browned and 165°F (74°C).
Cook the onion in the same pan for 4 minutes.
Warm the pita in a dry pan or the oven.
Fill with chicken, onion and tomato and drizzle with tahini.

ing: boiled and mashed, for potato filling
cooked and squeezed dry, for spinach filling
st: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
For a cheese filling, mix [[1 cup]] cheese with 1 egg and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
For a potato or spinach filling, mix [[1 cup]] mashed potato or [[2 cup]] cooked spinach with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and some of the cheese.
Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares.
Put a spoonful of filling in the center of each square.
Fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork to seal.
Beat 1 egg and brush the tops, then sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] sesame seeds.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve warm.
Pulse [[2 cup]] flour, [[1 cup]] butter, [[8 oz]] cream cheese and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a food processor until a dough forms.
Divide into 3 discs, wrap, and chill at least 1 hour.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] sugar with [[1 tbsp]] cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Roll one disc into a 10 inch circle and cut into 8 wedges.
Sprinkle the wedges with the cinnamon sugar and [[0.75 cup]] chocolate (split across the discs).
Roll each wedge from the wide end to the tip into a crescent.
Brush with the beaten egg and sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] sugar.
Bake 22 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool on a rack.
Whisk [[0.75 cup]] warm water, [[0.25 cup]] honey, [[0.25 cup]] oil and 2 eggs in a bowl.
Add [[4 cup]] flour, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and [[2 tsp]] salt. Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide the dough into 3 equal pieces and roll each into a 16 inch rope. Pinch the tops and braid, tucking the ends under.
Place on a lined tray and rise 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Brush with beaten yolk, sprinkle sesame seeds, and bake 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool before slicing.
nt: Best swap: use maple syrup for honey at the same amount, or add 1 more tbsp oil for extra richness.

st: Mix the flour, eggs, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[3 tbsp]] water until a dough forms. Knead 5 minutes until smooth, then wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until golden. Add the beef and cook until browned and fully cooked, with no pink, about 8 minutes.
Mince the beef mixture finely in a food processor with the pepper and remaining salt. Cool completely.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 3 inch squares.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the center, brush the edges with water, fold into a triangle and press tightly, then pinch the two long corners together.
Keep the broth hot at a simmer. Boil the kreplach in salted water for 8 minutes until they float.
Move them to bowls, ladle hot chicken broth over them, and add dill.
nt: Boiled, then served in chicken soup
Best swap: use ground chicken or mashed potato with fried onion for a lighter or meatless filling.

st: Line a small loaf pan with parchment and warm the tahini in a bowl for 20 seconds in the microwave so it is easy to stir.
Combine the sugar and water in a small pot over medium heat and stir until dissolved.
Boil without stirring until a candy thermometer reads exactly 240°F, about 8 minutes.
Pour the syrup quickly into the tahini with the vanilla and salt and stir with a spatula for 30 to 45 seconds, only until it thickens and starts to crumble.
Fold in the pistachios, press firmly into the pan and smooth the top.
Cool for 1 hour, then refrigerate overnight. Slice thin and bring to room temperature.
nt: Best swap: use sunflower seed butter in place of tahini for a nut and sesame free version, same quantity.

st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook the peppers 5 minutes, then add [[4 clove]] garlic, the paprika and jalapeno for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and sugar. Simmer uncovered 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mixture is thick and jammy and the oil separates. Salt it. This is matbucha.
Whisk the tahini with the juice of 1 lemon, [[1 clove]] garlic and a pinch of salt. It will stiffen. Add the ice water a spoon at a time until smooth and pourable.
Toss the cabbage with the juice of the second lemon, [[1 clove]] garlic, [[1 tbsp]] olive oil, the parsley and plenty of salt. Rub with your hands for 1 minute to soften it.
Let the cabbage rest 15 minutes, then taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Serve the matbucha, tahini and cabbage in small bowls with warm pita.
nt: Matbucha slow simmered in a skillet; tahini and cabbage salads are raw
Best swap: one 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes in place of the fresh ones in matbucha.

st: Mix the flour, warm milk, yeast, sugar, eggs and a pinch of salt. Knead in [[3 tbsp]] butter for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled. Roll out 1/2 inch thick and cut 12 rounds with a 3 inch cutter.
Rest the rounds on floured parchment 30 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oil to 350°F in a deep pot. Fry 3 or 4 doughnuts at a time, 1.5 minutes per side, until golden with a pale band round the middle.
Drain on paper towels. Fill a piping bag with [[0.75 cup]] jam, poke a hole in the side of each doughnut and pipe in about [[1 tbsp]] jam.
Dust with [[0.5 cup]] powdered sugar and serve the same day while still soft.
nt: Best swap: fill with dulce de leche or chocolate spread instead of jam, or bake at 375°F for 12 minutes for a lighter bun.

st: Grate the potatoes and onion on the large holes of a box grater. Pile them into a clean kitchen towel.
Twist the towel hard over the sink and squeeze out as much liquid as you can. Dry latkes are crisp latkes.
Mix the squeezed potato and onion with the eggs, matzo meal, salt and pepper in a bowl. Work quickly so the potatoes do not turn gray.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat until a shred of potato sizzles at once, about 350°F.
Drop [[2 tbsp]] of mixture per latke into the oil and press flat to about 3 inches wide. Fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp at the edges. Do not crowd the pan.
Drain on a rack set over a baking sheet or paper towels. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and keep warm in a 250°F oven while you fry the rest.
Serve hot with the applesauce and sour cream.
nt: Shallow fried in oil until crisp
Best swap: use 3 tbsp potato starch instead of matzo meal for gluten-free latkes, or bake at 425°F for 25 minutes.

st: Peel the lemons with a knife, cutting away all the white pith, which tastes bitter. Pick out any seeds.
Put the peeled lemons, mint, [[0.33 cup]] sugar and [[2 cup]] cold water into a strong blender.
Blend on high for 20 seconds only. Longer blending turns the mint bitter and the drink dark green.
Add [[3 cup]] ice cubes and blend 30 to 40 seconds until it is an icy, slushy green drink.
Taste and add a spoon of sugar if it is too sharp, then blend 5 seconds more.
Pour into tall glasses straight away, top with a mint sprig, and serve before the ice melts.
nt: Don't cook: just blend with ice
Best swap: [[0.5 cup]] lemon juice plus the zest of 1 lemon if you want to skip peeling whole lemons.
